Augusta leaders invite public to weigh in on proposed budget

By Staff
Published: Sep. 25, 2026 at 5:20 PM EDT|Updated: 18 hours ago
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:48
Instaread

AUGUSTA, Ga. (WRDW/WAGT) - Augusta officials are inviting residents to help shape the city’s spending plan for the coming year.

Members of the public can offer input through two public engagement sessions.

Augusta details $83.6M recovery push as Helene anniversary nears

Nearly two years after Hurricane Helene, Augusta officials say the city is closing in on getting most of its recovery costs reimbursed.

City Administrator Tameka Allen will lead the sessions, which are designed to give people a clearer look at Augusta’s budget priorities and how city dollars are spent.

Residents will also be able to ask questions.

When and where

In-person public engagement session (with livestream)

  • Date: Oct. 1
  • Location: Linda Beazley Room, 535 Telfair St.

Virtual public engagement session (with livestream)

  • Date: Oct. 5
  • Time: 6–7 p.m.
  • Online: Webinar link at AugustaGa.gov/FY2027Budget.

During the Oct. 5 webinar, residents can submit questions through the online link. Allen will respond in real time.
